about: Black Dirt Apple Jack comes out of Warwick Valley Winery & Distillery in Orange County, an hour north of Manhattan. The Grizzanti family bought an orchard there in 1989 and opened the winery to the public in 1994. Jason Grizzanti, the winemaker, and his partner Jeremy Kidde built a reputation for fruit brandies and liqueurs, then formed Black Dirt Distilling in 2012. The name honours the Black Dirt region nearby, a flat expanse of dark, fertile soil left on the bed of an ancient glacial lake.

Distilling began in 2013 in a 4,000-square-foot distillery on the winery grounds, with a 60-foot column still. The Apple Jack is made only from New York–grown Jonagold apples and aged at least four years in new charred American oak, the way a bourbon would be. It is bottled in bond: the product of one distillery and one distilling season, aged in a government-bonded warehouse and bottled at exactly 100 proof. Applejack is among the oldest American spirits, distilled by Northeastern farmers since colonial times.

The distillery describes a golden-honey colour, aromas of apple with caramel, cinnamon and sweet barrel spice, and a palate of baked apple and caramel touched with apricot and a sherry-like note, finishing sweet but balanced. The producer suggests it neat or over ice. Applejack is also the traditional base of the Jack Rose, the classic cocktail of applejack, lemon and grenadine.
